get_prospect_costs_light

Source: R/finance.R
get_prospect_costs_light.Rd

returns flexible and inflexible costs for each tariff_plan.

A lighter version of get_prospect_costs

get_prospect_costs_light(
  scen,
  kWh,
  phi,
  gamma,
  eta,
  tau,
  natural_profile = "LP1",
  smart_rollout,
  dyn_aware,
  prices_scen,
  params
)

Arguments

scen

scenario parameters

kWh

annual householdload

phi

\(\phi\)

gamma

\(\gamma\)

eta

\(\eta\)

tau

\(\tau\)

natural_profile

the characteristic profile of the household (currently LP1 or LP3)

smart_rollout

smart meter rollout time

dyn_aware

year of dynmaic choice awareness

prices_scen

price scenario

params

scenario parameters at yeartime

Value

a list with two elements: costs (a single-row tibble: flat, tou_noflex, tou_flex, det_noflex, det_flex) and profiles (a named list of hourly (datetime, price, load, load_opt, ...) tibbles, one per available plan flat has no load_opt since there's no shifting incentive on a flat tariff)

Details

the flat-tariff annual cost, and the tou/dynamic annual costs both with and without the household's optimal load-shifting response plus the underlying hourly load profiles themselves (original, tou-optimized, dynamic-optimized), not just the annual totals.

Unlike tariff_plan_bills() or get_annual_cost(), this does not discard get_flex() hourly output after summing it get_flex() is run once per available plan (tou, dynamic), and both the annual total and the hourly profile it produced are kept.

Plan availability at yeartime follows the same rule as tariff_plan_bills(): only flat before the household's smart meter rollout, flat+tou once rolled out but before dynamic pricing is introduced (2026.5), and all three plans after. Costs for plans that aren't yet available are NA; their profiles are simply absent from the returned list.

Examples

# sample values for standalone development/testing  in the real ABM these come from a
# specific agent's row (e.g. agents[1, ]) rather than being typed in by hand
prices_scen <- set_prices(sD)
params <- scenario_params(sD,2031)
get_prospect_costs_light(sD,kWh = 8760, phi = 0.4, gamma = 5, eta = 0.3, tau = 48,natural_profile = "LP1", smart_rollout = 2020,dyn_aware=2027, prices_scen,params)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>    flat tou_noflex tou_flex det_noflex det_flex
#>   <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 3336.      3400.    2794.      3453.    2823.
